name: Suez Canal Throughput and Rerouting Strain
title: Houthis–Saudi Arabia · Suez Canal Throughput and Rerouting Strain
situation: Red Sea and global shipping disruption

definition.question: How severely is Suez Canal throughput reduced and global rerouting strained?
definition.low_end: Suez Canal operates at normal capacity with stable transit numbers and no systemic rerouting of major trade lanes.
definition.high_end: Suez Canal traffic collapses with prolonged, large-scale rerouting of container and energy flows around the Cape of Good Hope, causing sustained global supply-chain delays and capacity shortages.

readings.rationale: No Suez-specific traffic, rerouting, or freight-rate data in evidence to place this dimension; Hormuz traffic drops and Houthi Bab el-Mandeb threat imply rerouting risk but do not verify Suez throughput. Research needed: Suez Canal Authority daily transits, major carrier rerouting announcements, and container freight indices. Would be higher if sustained 30%+ Suez drop and mass Cape rerouting…

No_change: still no Suez Canal Authority transit counts, carrier rerouting announcements, or freight-rate data to assess throughput; Hormuz 70% drop and Red Sea threat imply risk but do not verify Suez collapse.
